task.title: Reconcile selected active tools atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/639 by transitioning one explicit previous tool selection to one current selection as a single remove, replace, and add commit.
acceptance_criteria: Reject non-tool selections and build the complete descriptor-revalidated current adapter batch before mutation.
Atomically remove previous-only IDs, replace shared IDs, and add current-only IDs while preserving unrelated adapters.
Report deterministic duplicate, missing-previous, and unrelated-current conflict errors without partial mutation.
Preserve later per-invocation authorization, explicit limits, empty no-op behavior, and caller-owned lifecycle evidence.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for one mixed lifecycle transition.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused kernel and extension tests could not compile because no reconciliation error, registry primitive, or previous-to-current extension operation existed.
attempts.patch: Added tests for mixed success, deterministic preflight failures, current artifact failure, collisions, wrong kinds, empty selections, and explicit invocation limits.

attempts.diagnostic: Explicit previous ownership plus a fully built current batch lets one registry preflight distinguish removals, replacements, additions, and unrelated collisions before mutation.
attempts.patch: Added ToolRegistry::reconcile_all, typed kernel and extension errors, default and limit-aware reconciliation operations, docs, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Added direct evidence against sequential partial state during independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: Success and rollback tests did not by themselves show why composing deactivation and activation was insufficient when the second operation failed.
attempts.patch: Added a regression demonstrating that sequential deactivation followed by failed activation loses the old adapter, then verified the atomic operation preserves it.

outcome.summary: Caller-owned previous and current tool selections now drive one atomic remove, replace, and add transition that preserves every old and unrelated adapter on failure.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30228966755 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/640

lessons: Sequentially correct lifecycle operations can still expose partial state when composed across a later failure.
Adapter ownership must come from explicit caller-held previous selection evidence rather than registry inference.
A current-only ID needs distinct conflict handling because an existing adapter may be unrelated to the reconciled selection.
Rebuilding shared IDs uniformly keeps current-root artifact revalidation simple and avoids an unproven optimization.

CodeRabbit suggested renaming the public root parameter to current_root in pull request 640; the non-blocking suggestion was not applied before merge, while the API documentation retained the contract that only the complete current batch is revalidated.
